answer:
1. Document requirements
2. Choose appropriate media
3. Plan cable runs (stay under 100m for copper)
4. Label everything
5. Test all connections
6. Document the network diagram
7. Verify functionality
T568A: Green/White-Green, Orange/White-Orange, Blue/White-Blue, Brown/White-Brown, Brown (pins 1-8). T568B: Orange/White-Orange, Green/White-Green, Blue/White-Blue, Brown/White-Brown.
Used to connect different device types (e.g., PC to switch, switch to router). Same wiring on both ends (T568A-A or T568B-B). Most common cable type in modern networks.
Used to connect same device types (e.g., switch to switch, PC to PC). One end T568A, other T568B. Modern NICs auto-MDI-X so crossover may not be needed.
Connects computer serial port to console port of router/switch. Pin 1 to pin 8, reversed. Used for out-of-band management and initial device configuration.
Entrance Facility, Backbone Cabling, Telecommunications Room, Horizontal Cabling, Work Area. MDF (Main Distribution Frame) and IDF (Intermediate Distribution Frame).
Plenum: Fire-retardant jacket for air handling spaces (HVAC), more expensive. PVC: Standard jacket, cheaper but produces toxic fumes when burning. Use plenum in ceiling spaces.
LC: Small form factor, most common in data centers. SC: Subscriber connector, square. ST: Straight tip, bayonet twist. FC: Fiber optic connector, screw-type. MTRJ: Mechanical transfer ribbon.

Single-mode (SMF): 9μm core, laser, long distance (up to 70km+). Multi-mode (MMF): 50/62.5μm core, LED, short distance (up to 550m). Never bend fiber below minimum bend radius. Clean connectors with isopropyl alcohol.
Create VLANs, configure trunk ports, set native VLAN, enable PortFast on access ports, configure spanning tree, set management IP, enable SSH, configure port security.
Limits number of MAC addresses on a switch port. Violation modes: Shutdown (default - disables port), Restrict (drops frames), Protect (drops frames silently). Prevents unauthorized device access.
Set hostname, configure interfaces with IP addresses and subnet masks, enable routing protocols (static, RIP, OSPF, EIGRP), configure NAT/PAT, set up SSH, configure DHCP relay.
Link-state routing protocol. Uses Dijkstra SPF algorithm. Area 0 (backbone) required. Hello interval 10 sec (Ethernet), Dead interval 40 sec. Administrative distance: 110. Supports VLSM and CIDR.
Cisco-proprietary hybrid (distance-vector + link-state). Uses DUAL algorithm. Fast convergence, supports unequal-cost load balancing. Administrative distance: 90. Supports VLSM.

Distance-vector protocol. Maximum 15 hops (16 = unreachable). RIP v1: classful, RIP v2: classless (supports VLSM/multicast). Administrative distance: 120. Slow convergence, not suitable for large networks.
Manually configured routes. Best for simple networks or stub networks. Administrative distance: 1 (most trusted). No overhead, no routing protocol traffic. Used for default routes and backup routes.
Gateway of last resort (0.0.0.0/0). Used when no specific route matches the destination. Configured with `ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 <next-hop>` or `ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 <exit-interface>`.
Static route with a higher administrative distance than a dynamic protocol. Used as a backup route. If the dynamic route fails, the floating static route is installed in the routing table.
Static NAT: One-to-one mapping. Dynamic NAT: Pool of public IPs. PAT (Overload): Many-to-one mapping using port numbers. Configured with access lists and `ip nat inside/outside` commands.
Configure switchport mode trunk, set allowed VLANs, set native VLAN (ideally not VLAN 1), enable DTP (Dynamic Trunking Protocol) or manually configure trunk. Use `show interfaces trunk` to verify.
Set SSID, choose security protocol (WPA2-Enterprise), configure VLAN assignment, set channel and transmit power, enable Fast Roaming (802.11r), configure RADIUS authentication.
Leased Line (dedicated point-to-point), MPLS (provider-managed, QoS), DSL (ADSL/VDSL over copper), Cable (DOCSIS), Fiber (PON), Satellite (high latency), Cellular (4G/5G).
Uses labels to forward packets through a provider network. PE (Provider Edge) and CE (Customer Edge) routers. Supports VPN, QoS, and traffic engineering. Connection-oriented at Layer 2.5.
Data link protocol for serial connections. Provides authentication (PAP/CHAP), encryption (MPPE), and compression. LCP (Link Control Protocol) and NCP (Network Control Protocol) layers.

PAP (Password Authentication Protocol): 2-way handshake, sends credentials in cleartext, no protection against replay. CHAP (Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol): 3-way handshake, uses MD5 hash, periodically re-authenticates.

Cable certifier: Tests all pairs for length, attenuation, crosstalk, impedance. Time-domain reflectometer (TDR): Locates cable faults (breaks, shorts). Wire map tester: Verifies pinout continuity. Fluke meters are industry standard.

PDU (Power Distribution Unit): Distributes power to equipment. UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply): Battery backup for short outages. Generator: Long-term backup. PD (Power Distribution) units in data centers manage circuit loads.

Temperature: 64-75°F (18-24°C) recommended for data centers. Humidity: 40-60% relative humidity. Fire suppression: FM-200, clean agent systems (not water). Airflow: Hot aisle/cold aisle configuration.
MDF (Main Distribution Frame): Central point for backbone connections, network equipment. IDF (Intermediate Distribution Frame): Distribution point on each floor, connects horizontal cabling to MDF.
Wiring diagrams, network topology maps, device inventory, IP address allocation tables, documentation of cable runs and IDF/MDF locations, change management logs.
